summary:
Space Exploration Game Design Summary
​1. Onboarding & Spacecraft Engineering
Players begin with an interactive tutorial workshop to master game mechanics and spacecraft engineering. Starting at Level 1, players manage a strict budget to build their ship, selecting specific hull materials and designing an ocean-landing escape pod for safe Earth re-entry.
​2. Resource Calculation & Test Flights
Before launching, players must calculate essential survival and operational resources based on mission distance: oxygen, fuel, food, and power (choosing between battery storage or solar panels). Players then conduct test flights to verify their ship's structural integrity and flight stability.
​3. Planetary Missions & HQ Support
Level 1 players start with low-reward missions to nearby planets. During flight, Earth HQ provides an AI assistant that tracks real-time coordinates and scans for nearby hazards. Along the journey, players face random challenges like dodging space debris.
​4. Exploration, Extraction & Progression
Upon landing, players deploy specialized equipment—such as rovers, robots, or vacuum hoovers—to explore the terrain and collect alien soil samples. Returning safely via the ocean escape pod completes the mission. Players earn financial rewards and experience points to level up, unlocking advanced materials and allowing them to engineer stronger spacecraft for deeper space exploration.

Project Details: Orbital Ledger

Orbital Ledger is a hardcore, NASA-synchronized space exploration and aerospace engineering simulation available on PC and mobile devices.

  • Onboarding & Training: Players register via social accounts or guest mode, customize their astronaut avatar, and graduate from the NASA Astronaut Training Camp by mastering spacecraft systems, high-G training, microgravity survival, and emergency protocols. Players can explore solo or in squads of up to four.
  • Agency Management: Starting with baseline capital, players accept Mission Control contracts for funds and EXPto upgrade NASA-modeled facilities. Advancing unlocks higher-difficulty missions and replay cycles with rare sample collection and increased failure risks.
  • Spacecraft Engineering: Design rockets using an in-game 3D model library and official NASA specs. Synthesize raw materials into sub-components, assemble internal systems (structural, propulsion, GNC, electrical, TT&C, payload) and physical staging (boosters, core stages, fairings), equip separation mechanisms (explosive bolts, LSC, Marman clamps), and pass pre-launch escape velocity tests.
  • Surface Exploration: Configure lunar and Martian rovers (Apollo LRVs, LTVs, Pressurized Rovers) featuring thermal insulation, airless metal mesh wheels, and Rocker-Bogie suspensions.
  • Mission Planning & Orbits: Use a 3D Solar System Orrery, waypoint mapping, and Hohmann transfer calculations to plan trajectories. Pre-test mission plans inside upgradable Simulation Chambers.
  • Campaigns & Operations: Experience historical and modern space programs (Mercury, Gemini, Apollo, ISS, Artemis, and robotic deep-space probes). Manage 5-phase flight operations, ISS 24-hour UTC routines, and post-flight physiological recovery (including NASA's 45-day ASCR rehabilitation protocol for microgravity effects).
  • Crises & Penalties: Survive authentic NASA-probability emergencies (such as lightning strikes, space debris, solar flares, and computer crashes) within strict countdown timers. Mission failures deduct 25% of total funds, and reaching 100 million in debt triggers bankruptcy and Game Over. Successful returns award scores on a Top 100 Leaderboard, complemented by Competitive Scenarios and a Sandbox Mode.
projectRefs: After completing the design, the player launches the satellite through an animated sequence. The game then presents the resulting spacecraft configuration and provides scientific results based on the player's design. It also identifies real NASA missions with similar characteristics and scientific objectives, allowing the player to relate their virtual design to actual space missions.
